transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m pretty sure the people at my apartment are watching when I come and go. They’re slipping notes about me to the office, and everybody keeps saying it’s just regular notices on the doors, but that’s not how it feels to me.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
I don’t think so. I mean, I hear noises in the building sometimes, but not voices talking to me when nobody’s there.
When did you first start feeling that the people at your apartment were watching you?
It started a little over a year ago... maybe about a year and a month. That’s when I really started feeling like the neighbors and the office were keeping track of me.
During this time, have you had a period when you felt unusually depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yes. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already gone bad before I even get out of bed. It’s there a lot of the day.
Have you found yourself losing interest or motivation to do the things you used to do?

Yeah, I have. I used to look forward to choir practice, playing bridge, cooking beans on Sundays… even doing little repair jobs for people. Now I mostly just let the phone ring and tell myself there’s no point in going.
Have there been times when you still felt watched even when you were not feeling depressed?

Yes. There was a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling quite as low—I was eating a little better and not waking up so hopeless. But even then, I still felt like the neighbors were watching my door and telling somebody about me.
Have you ever believed that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside of you?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in my mind exactly. What I do know is I came in because I’m sure the people at my apartment are watching when I come and go, and they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody says they’re just regular notices on the doors, but that’s not how it feels to me.
Have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?
I’m not really sure. I guess I don’t talk as much as I used to, but I haven’t been paying close attention to it. Some days I just don’t feel like saying much.
Has there been a time when you felt watched like this for at least two weeks while you were not feeling depressed?

Yes. It went on for several weeks. I wasn’t feeling as depressed then—I was eating a little better and not waking up feeling so hopeless—but I still thought the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me.
Have you found yourself showing much less emotion on your face or in your voice than you used to?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my face or voice being different like that. I mean, I might seem flat sometimes when I’m tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than before.
Has a doctor ever told you that you have a brain or nervous system illness, like epilepsy, a head injury, or dementia?
Not that I know of. No doctor has told me I have something like epilepsy or dementia or a brain injury.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric?
I don’t think so. I can’t really remember a time where I felt unusually high or euphoric like that.
Have these beliefs that your neighbors are watching you been present for at least one month?
Yes. It’s been longer than a month. I’d say those thoughts about the neighbors and the office have been going on for about a year… maybe a year and a month.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?

Yes, some people have said that. When I’m trying to explain something, I’ll start talking about the rent, then I’m on to the marina, then the choir robes, and the wires in the walls… and people look at me like I skipped over half the story. I don’t always notice it until I see their face.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really seen things that other people couldn’t see, not that I can remember.
During the past year that these beliefs about your neighbors have been going on, have you felt depressed for most of that time?

Yes. Most of that time since I moved, I’ve felt pretty low. Even on days where I could talk a little clearer or seem okay, underneath I still felt useless and didn’t really care about doing the things I used to like.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms, including persecutory delusions and disorganized speech, present for over 1 month and overall about a year. A major depressive syndrome was present for most of the illness course with depressed mood and marked loss of interest. Crucially, psychotic symptoms also persisted for several weeks in the absence of depression, supporting schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, rather than psychotic depression alone. No history of manic or hypomanic episodes was endorsed, and no neurological cause was reported.
